title: Grassroots Leadership Training: Launch an Action Team to Build Electoral Power in Racine County
description:
How can you fight back against the extreme Republican agenda and create a better future where everyone in Wisconsin can thrive? Become a leader of a neighborhood action team! 

Since 2017, neighborhood action teams have been monumental in electing Democrats in close races in Wisconsin. That’s why we’re launching teams in Racine County to take our organizing to the next level! By building community and having powerful conversations with our neighbors this summer, we’ll be prepared to take on Republicans and win elections up and down the ballot in 2026. 

Through this training, you will learn the skills and strategy to effectively launch and lead your neighborhood action team. Plus, you’ll be matched with other motivated co-leaders in your area to work together and receive ongoing support from the Democratic Party of Wisconsin.

Note: This training is designed for volunteers who can commit to being a co-leader of a neighborhood action team in Caledonia, Mt. Pleasant, or the city of Racine. title: Art Against the Power Grab: Storytelling Action in Mountain View

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

description:
Trump’s administration is in full-on power grab mode, shredding laws, defying courts, and handing control of the country’s financial system to a billionaire crony. We need all-out, relentless pressure to stop this coup in its tracks.

One of the key ways to win is to **spread the word of how these horrible cuts and policies have already affected people**. A 2-year-old cancer patient who is a US citizen deported. An 11-year-old Texas girl who took her life after being bullied by her classmates who threatened to contact ICE. A former Marine and forest ranger who saved countless lives, fired. All these stories – we can help tell them.

At NC Story Tellers event, WI Dem Party Chair Ben Wikler said: Telling stories of the people whose lives were affected is how we win. By putting names, faces, and emotions to the issues, we define the battle lines and force the question: whose side are you on? Stories make it a moral issue, and they do so in a way nothing else can; that’s how we’re wired as humans. This approach is key to holding Trump accountable for the damage, chaos, and destruction his administration is causing. This is how we win back the statehouses and state supreme courts, end gerrymandering, and restore democracy in the United States.

Inspired by the **AIDS Quilt project** (which used art to spread awareness of the AIDS epidemic), we will create posters to tell the stories of the people whose lives were made worse by the Trump administration. These art projects that can be as simple or as elaborate as your skills allow. 

This is step 1 (step 2, scheduled separately: a visibility event using these posters).

title: Sign the Petition for SB1 Referendum in Delphos
description:
We'll be at Stadium Park in Delphos with the Van Wert Dems to collect signatures for the referendum on SB1. 

## WHAT IS SENATE BILL 1?

- Senate Bill 1  (“The Higher Education Destruction Act”) was signed into OH law by Gov. DeWine on March 28, 2025 and goes into effect on June 25, 2025. 
- SB1 guts collective bargaining rights for faculty unions, removes job protections for educators & bans striking time for full-time staff.
- SB1 allows colleges & universities to end programs & terminate faculty positions without warning or cause.
- SB1 bans most diversity, equity & inclusion programs and staff training in higher education.
- We have until June 22 to collect 250,000 signatures in OH and get a repeal measure on the Nov. ballot.
- Republicans in OH leadership have now introduced bills (SB113 & HB155) targeted at grades K-12. We must stop attacks on public education!
- For more information, visit [ohiosb1petition.com](ohiosb1petition.com)
- Sign the petition to repeal SB1!

title: A Funeral for the Constitution - A Peaceful Protest of the Inaction of Senator Thom Tillis
description:
Join us on August 23, we will gather in downtown Greensboro dressed in black, not in celebration - but in mourning.
This solemn protest, led by concerned citizens across North Carolina, is a funeral march for our Constitution - the foundational document Senator Thom Tillis continues to undermine and nullify, piece by piece.
As we carry a symbolic coffin through the streets, accompanied by the haunting sound of a lone bagpipe, we will grieve the erosion of civil liberties, voting rights, and democratic norms. This is not a spectacle. This is a eulogy - for fairness, for accountability, and for a government of the people.

With peaceful resolve and powerful symbolism, we will honor what has been lost and demand better from those elected to serve us. We mourn, we march, and we resist - because democracy should not die in silence.

title: Get in Line, Senator Tillis

While he continues to ignore the will of his constituents, we're responding not with silence, but with rhythm, joy and movement! Our feet will hit the ground in Guilford County on July 12, where every step is a stand - a stand for community building, for kindness, and for those whose voices have been sidelined.

With music, unity and purpose, we're turning this protest into a celebration and resistance into motion! Join us - because when we move together, we shift the future, and we won't stop dancing until our representatives fall in line with the people they serve!

title: Heartland Wins Canvass
description:
What issues will bring voters out in the 2026 midterm election? Let's ask them!

Join us on Saturday, June 21st, to talk to voters and start doing the real work to flip Missouri's Second Congressional district. We will be meeting in the Ellisville/Chesterfield area at 11am. The location and address will be provided closer to the date for privacy reasons.

We will provide everything else you will need, and we will have plenty of people on hand to train everyone if needed!

Paid for by Heartland Wins and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee

description:
#### Sorting Soup: Turning Ideas Into Action - Join Weekly - every Tuesday & Thursday,  Zoom @4PM central

_Feeling overwhelmed by the constant stream of ideas, strategies, and information in the pro-democracy movement? You’re not alone._

That’s why we created Sorting Soup—a twice-weekly space to process, connect, and turn information into real-world impact. Inspired by the dynamic NWSOFA 9am Coffee & Conversation network, Sorting Soup is your opportunity to ground yourself, build community, and decide what’s truly worth your time and energy.

#### Let us know you will be attending … RSVP here-> https://mobilize.us/s/1162kb

Join us every Tuesday and Thursday at 4 PM (CST), starting June 10th. Each session begins with a Decompression Hour, where we check in, share what’s on our minds, and spot the patterns emerging across our work. Then, we dive deep into a timely topic—something urgent, overlooked, or full of potential. Whether you’re ready to research, present, or just ask great questions, your voice is welcome.

We wrap up with a Deep Dive Debrief, assigning research tasks, brainstorming future speakers, and mapping out next steps. Our goal? Not just understanding, but activation. Sorting Soup is about thinking together—and then bringing those insights back to our communities to inspire real change.

Indivisible Baltimore is starting a book club so that we can educate ourselves about the systems we struggle against and the tactics that are most effective. Our first pick will be The Sum of Us: What Racism Costs Everyone and How We Can Prosper Together, by Heather McGhee.

We encourage you to order your copy from Urban Reads Bookstore, a local, Black-owned business that has been targeted recently by white supremacists. You can of course, also get it from the library or listen to the audio. 

June is extremely busy so we are holding it on Father's Day June 15. We understand this may mean not everyone can attend, but it's important for us to fit it in before Leah Greenberg has her allyship meeting with Heather McGhee on June 24 from 4:00-5:30pm. 

Since we have introduced this topic so quickly, we realize many won't have time to read the entire book yet so we will use this first meeting to introduce the main ideas of the book, and introduce ourselves.

When we meet in July, we will be discussing the book after you have read it (hopefully).
